data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject rather than describes it only when the test installation mechanism changes the subject's failure semantics before the test executes \u2014 shown-to-fail-first installation does exactly this because it makes the guard's own failure a precondition for the guard to be registered as a test subject.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the installation order is randomized and the result is invariant, the test describes rather than constrains.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If every ordinarily-guarded module showed the same 1/9 loss rate, the effect is systematic description not constraint.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If compile.py mutations are drawn from the same distribution as module mutations, the 3-of-26 result is a description of mutation space.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"In shown-to-fail-first installation, a mutation that fails the guard's own test is recorded as 'lost' before the ordinarily-guarded module's mutation tests run. The guard's failure becomes a filter on what counts as a testable subject, so the test constrains the population of mutations it can see rather than describing an independent distribution.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
